title: Reported Speech Quiz 2
description: Change the pronouns, the time words and the place words when the point of view changes.
topic: Pronouns, time words and place words
instructions: Reported Speech: Pronouns, time words and place words.
Imagine that every report is made on a later day and in a different place.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: 'I will see you tomorrow,' Ann said to Tom. Which report is correct?
options: Ann told Tom she would see you the next day.
Ann told Tom I would see him tomorrow.
Ann told Tom she would see him the next day.
Ann told Tom she will see him tomorrow.
questions.explanation: I becomes she, you becomes him, will becomes would, and tomorrow becomes the next day. Watch out: you cannot stay, because the listener is now he.

questions.question: 'We are leaving now,' they said. They said ___
questions.explanation: We becomes they, are leaving becomes were leaving, and now becomes then. Watch out: we and now both point to the old situation.

questions.question: 'I lost my bag here yesterday,' he said. → He said he {{1}} his bag {{2}} the day before.
questions.explanation: Lost becomes had lost, here becomes there, and yesterday becomes the day before. Watch out: here does not stay when the place changes.

questions.question: 'We will visit our aunt next week,' they said. → They said they would visit their aunt {{1}}.
questions.explanation: Next week becomes the following week or the week after. Watch out: next week stays only when the report is made in the same week.

questions.question: In 'I lost my keys,' said Tom, the word my becomes his in the report.
questions.explanation: The possessive follows the speaker, so my becomes his. Watch out: it stays my only when Tom himself makes the report.

questions.question: Report this: 'I met him two days ago,' she said.
options: She said she met him two days ago.
She said she had met him two days after.
She said she had met him in two days.
She said she had met him two days before.
questions.explanation: Ago becomes before, and met becomes had met. Watch out: after would point forward, not back.

questions.question: Choose the reported time word or phrase.
questions.explanation: Time words are measured from the moment of speaking, so they move away from now. Watch out: tomorrow becomes the next day, and yesterday becomes the day before.

questions.question: Match each word with its reported form.
questions.explanation: Words of place and distance move away from the speaker. Watch out: ago becomes before, not after.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The subject, the reporting verb, then the clause with would and the time phrase last. Watch out: the next day goes at the end.

questions.question: 'You are late,' Tom said to Ann. Tom told Ann that ___ late.
questions.explanation: You refers to Ann, so for a third-person reporter it becomes she, and are becomes was. Watch out: you would stay only if Ann herself made the report.

questions.question: Which changes are correct?
questions.explanation: Pronouns follow the speaker and time words move back. Watch out: yesterday cannot become the next day, and today does not become this day.

questions.question: Correct the mistake (the report is made a week later): He said he would come tomorrow.
accepted: He said he would come the next day.
He said he would come the next day
He said he would come the following day.
He said he would come the following day
He said he would come the day after.
He said he would come the day after
questions.explanation: Tomorrow becomes the next day or the following day. Watch out: tomorrow would point to a day after the report.
